en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Gabbhinīvagga 69.
The Training Rule on Following a Female Leader.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs did not follow their appointed mentor (pavattinī) for two years after she had been ordained.
They were foolish and incompetent;
they did not know what was allowable or what was unallowable.
Those bhikkhunīs who were few in desires... they complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these bhikkhunīs not follow their preceptor for two years after she has given her the full admission? ...
"Is it true, monks, that bhikkhunīs do not follow their preceptor for two years after she has given her the full admission?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, monks, can nuns not follow their preceptor for two years after she has been ordained?”
“Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And thus, monks, should the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:
‘If a bhikkhunī does not follow her preceptor for two years after she has been ordained, it is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).’”
"But whichever" means whichever such...
"nun" means... [as before].
...pe... this is the nun intended in this context.
"Ordained" means fully admitted into the order.
The term "Pavattinī" refers to the preceptor (upajjhāyā).
"Two years" means...
Two years.
"Should not follow" means she should not attend upon him herself.
If she thinks, "I will not follow [her] for two years," there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) at the mere moment of relinquishing the burden.
There is no offense if the preceptor is foolish or shameless.
For one who is ill,
in cases of emergency,
for one who is insane,
"By one who is a first offender.
The ninth training rule is concluded.
